settings.description: Only non-dialogue cards are eligible for automatic music.
Missing, empty, unreadable, or ineligible libraries do not block completion.
The repository-root Music directory is referenced read-only.
Tracks are never looped automatically.
Eligible tracks are selected deterministically by content digest order.
Bundled local music is restricted to internal outputs.
Separate broadcast reference profile target.
Background music under programme dialogue is disabled by default.
If dialogue music is enabled it is ducked by this amount.
Hum reduction is not applied without explicit enablement.
Hum reduction may be proposed for review.
Internal and online loudness tolerance is plus or minus one decibel.
Internal and online talk output uses the product-adopted target.
Loudness and true peak are measured with BS.1770-5.
Digest ordering does not establish musical or brand fit.
Noise reduction is not applied without explicit enablement.
Noise reduction may be proposed for review.
Mechanical ducking does not prove perceptual speech understanding.
Quick start selects the internal and online talk profile, not broadcast.
Short self-generated sound effects mark topic changes and emphasis captions at a low level.
True peak must not exceed minus one dBFS.
Only adjacent same-speaker NFKC exact repetitions may be auto-excluded.
A short uses the single text 本編を見る only when a corresponding long-form version exists; otherwise it has no call to action. No URL or other action is inferred.
Context deviation remains a review candidate and is not auto-removed.
Cough observations remain review candidates and are not auto-removed.
A deliberately enabled crossfade uses a short product-defined duration.
Crossfade is disabled by default.
Explicit cut phrases may be excluded while preserving source and reason.
Zero milliseconds means no transition rather than an external recommendation.
Standard applies only closed deterministic edits automatically.
J and L cuts derive length from speech and silence boundaries.
Jump-cut mitigation uses only approved source-grounded visuals.
Long-form opener media is disabled by default.
Noise observations remain review candidates and are not auto-removed.
Pauses between utterances of at least 2 s (weak), 0.7 s (standard) or 0.4 s (strong) are shortened, keeping 0.15 s on each side.
Normal picture joins use a hard cut.
Fuzzy and semantic repetition matching cannot trigger automatic deletion.
A source-grounded hook may start within the first three seconds by default; one to five seconds can be chosen.
A hook is allowed only when supported by the original utterance.
Short-form opener media is disabled by default.
Leading and trailing silence of at least two seconds is detected.
Three tenths of a second is retained around speech.
The adopted Stage 0 silence detector threshold is minus fifty dB.
Large topic boundaries prefer a title card rather than crossfade.
The default evaluation mode is explicitly automated proxy evaluation.
Automated results must not be labeled as human evaluation pass.
Single-user self-review remains optional.
Mono stays mono and stereo stays stereo without synthesizing channels.
The conservative output audio codec is AAC-LC.
Output audio uses a 48 kHz sample rate.
The conservative local output container is MP4.
Quick start produces local files and does not post directly.
Eligible videos reserve five seconds for an end screen.
End screens apply only to videos at least twenty-five seconds long.
No external platform upload or organic-posting compliance is claimed.
Frame rate follows the source rather than a fixed 30000 over 1001 value.
HDR quick-start input is explicitly tone-mapped to SDR BT.709.
HDR tone mapping always records a visible warning.
1080p at 48, 50, or 60 fps uses twelve megabits per second.
The production landscape output is 1920 by 1080.
A portrait source produces a portrait 1080 by 1920 long-form version; a landscape source keeps 1920 by 1080.
Preserved mono output uses 128 kbps.
SDR output uses BT.709.
The separate vertical Shorts classification ceiling is three minutes.
Short selection targets thirty seconds within a fifteen-to-sixty-second search range.
1080p at 24, 25, or 30 fps uses eight megabits per second.
Preserved stereo output uses 384 kbps.
The production vertical output is 1080 by 1920 without a platform-compliance claim.
Video uses H.264 High Profile, progressive scan, and 4:2:0 chroma.
Cloud payloads are limited to explicitly selected and masked transcript spans.
Cloud text suggestions are disabled by default.
Cross-account isolation is not claimed by the initial release scope.
External publication is outside the initial release scope.
Initial use is scoped to one current Windows standard user.
The active standard Windows user is the sole initial user.
Performer names and titles are not inferred.
Language is detected and falls back to ja-JP when indeterminate.
No publication deadline is invented.
Quick-start projects and outputs are internal only.
Quick start creates the standard local artifact candidate set.
One source video is the only required project input.
Applied defaults are summarized before editing starts.
The production default is a neutral built-in template with no logo.
Quick start requests at most three vertical short candidates.
No retention duration is invented and automatic deletion stays off.
No backup destination is assumed.
Backup is manual until a destination is explicitly chosen.
The default workspace is a writable per-user local application data path.
Subtitle background is solid black.
Subtitle background is opaque.
Adjacent cues have a minimum two-frame gap.
Sub-half-second gaps close to two frames and longer gaps are retained.
Primary subtitle cues are at most seven seconds long.
Primary subtitle cues use the canonical five-sixths-second minimum.
How many short emphasis captions are shown for key phrases: few, standard or many.
Prerecorded quick-start outputs include subtitle candidates.
Subtitle foreground is white.
Japanese SDH-oriented horizontal text is limited to sixteen full-width characters.
Landscape authored line height is seven and one-half percent.
Landscape subtitles fall back to the BBC generic central region.
Landscape output includes burn-in, clean, SRT, and VTT variants.
Line breaks prefer natural syntactic boundaries.
Primary subtitles use at most two lines.
The generic region is not a TikTok, YouTube, or LinkedIn compliance claim.
An unmeasured platform mask falls back to the generic BBC subtitle region.
No platform-specific UI mask is treated as measured.
Use of the generic fallback always emits a warning.
The default is an SDH-oriented candidate and not an SDH conformance claim.
Japanese SDH-oriented candidates use a seven full-width-character-per-second maximum.
Speaker and non-speech semantic completeness is not automatically established.
Normal translation subtitles share the canonical five-sixths-second minimum.
Normal Japanese translation subtitles use thirteen full-width characters per horizontal line.
Normal translation subtitles use at most two lines.
Normal translation subtitles remain a separate profile.
Normal Japanese translation subtitles use a four-character-per-second maximum.
Normal Japanese translation subtitles use eleven full-width characters per vertical line.
Vertical quick-start output burns subtitles into the picture.
Vertical authored line height is four and one-fifth percent.
Japanese SDH-oriented vertical text is limited to eleven full-width characters.
Vertical subtitles fall back to the BBC generic central region.
Up to three thumbnail candidates are generated for selection; one to three can be chosen.
Generated faces are not allowed in thumbnail candidates.
Generated scenes are not allowed in thumbnail candidates.
Landscape thumbnail canvas is 1280 by 720 as a product default.
Thumbnail imagery comes only from actual source video frames.
Thumbnail text remains short and accurately represents the video.
Vertical thumbnail canvas is 1080 by 1920.
